prerequisites: deep knowledge of the organization of modern computer architectures
good programming capabilities using the C language

learning_outcomes.text: Know and understand the architecture of the different types of operating systems in terms of their components, and the related functionalities, related to the different devices where they are deployed.
Know and understand the main characteristics of the UNIX/Linux operating system families.
Know and understand the main characteristics of mobile and embedded operating system, and, in particular, of the Android operating system.
Know and understand the basic concepts behind virtualization technologies and cloud computing.
Know and understand the main issues that need to be analyzed for designing and managing an operating system.
Use the basic operating system library functions used in application programming for managing processes and threads.
Use the techniques to correctly configure an operating system according to the device and the application scenario at hand.
Choose the most apt operating system given the set of requirements related to the application scenario at hand.
Explain in an organic way the dependences among the different modules of an operating systems, and the dependences of these modules on the device where they have been deployed.
Understand the technical documentation that is published by developers and producers of operating systems, especially the one related to open source projects.

syllabus_topics: Main components of modern operating systems
The Linux OS: system structure, file system organization, basic commands, shell scripting basics
Mutual exclusion, process synchronization and deadlock
Input/Output systems, file system and disk management
Elements of mobile and embedded operating systems
teaching_methods: lectures with electronic presentations (PowerPoint or similar)
lab exercises using the Linux operating systems
lab exercises on various aspects of modern operating systems and virtualization platforms
a seminar or a site visit

assessment_methods.method: written test (open questions, numerical exercises, programming exercises)
short oral test (optional, to increase final mark)

assessment_rules: The written test will be considered valid if an answer is provided to each question. For each exercise/question, a maximum score is assigned, and evaluated from 0 to the maximum based on correctness and severity of errors. The final mark is the sum of points assigned, with a total of 32 points for '30 cum laude'. It is possible to increase the final mark with a short oral test.
